claim: OpenAJS (cubk1/OpenAJS, created 2026-06-07) is the only public repository found that reimplements the FV tunnel end-to-end rather than driving the official client.
The control API is HTTP POST to /client.php with an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body of sorted key=value pairs, plus headers X-Timestamp and X-Sig and User-Agent okhttp/4.9.3.
The X-Sig value is hex(dualHash(secret + "|" + body + "|" + timestamp + "|" + secret)); dualHash is two 32-bit rolling hashes (65599 multiplier and 32*x+x>>2 xor) emitted as 8 interleaved bytes.
OpenAJS ships four candidate API hosts: login.ajs-app.com, login.mmegg.com, login.mmegg.com:4443 and login.mbclubsh.com, tried in order.
ajs-app.com is independently recognised as an AJiaSu domain by a third-party proxy rule-set (DOMAIN-SUFFIX,ajs-app.com alongside 91ajs.com).

FV authentication frame = 16-byte IV || AES-CTR(headerIV, zeroIV) over a 4-byte header (2 reserved bytes, 2-byte text length) plus the text s=/n=/k=/l=/_=; k is the literal ASCII 'OAEP' followed by RSA-OAEP(sessionKey).

The FV auth body is newline-delimited key=value text (c=au, u, p, cuid, cseid, st, v, cv=20260525-1, osp, osd, osv, dim, ce) encrypted with AES-CTR under a random 16-byte sessionKey and 16-byte bodyIV.
A successful auth response carries r=ok and sid; subsequent data channels reuse the same sessionKey with a fresh 16-byte IV per TCP connection and send an empty k= field.
The FV data channel begins with a raw SOCKS5 CONNECT request (VER=5, CMD=1, ATYP=3 domain name) and the server answers with a header containing code=200 followed by a 10-byte SOCKS5 reply.
OpenAJS's local SOCKS5 server is bound to 127.0.0.1 only, offers no authentication and rejects any command other than CONNECT with reply 0x07.
OpenAJS disables TLS certificate and hostname verification globally, so that client implements no certificate pinning; whether the official clients pin certificates is [UNKNOWN].

The Linux client is driven by subcommands login / list / connect and an /etc/ajiasu.conf holding user, pass, protocol, cache_dir, connect, use_vpn_dns and use_vpn_route; protocol values include udp, tcp, lwip, proxy (and socks5/http per dnomd343).
The Linux client's local proxy listens on 127.0.0.1:1080 by default; the config file has no port field, so a second instance drifts to the next free port.
Parallel Linux client instances are achievable by giving each a distinct cache_dir and --sys-env-id; the listener port must then be discovered at runtime.

In client 4.2.3.0 the SOCKS5 handshake was reported unusable while the HTTP proxy mode worked, whereas 4.1.1.0-era scripts used socks5h successfully; the SOCKS5 data path is therefore version-dependent.
A single ajiasu client process holds at most one active node connection; this is a per-process constraint, not an account-wide one (see C21).
Official client matrix as of 2026-10-23: Windows 4.9.6.0, macOS 4.9.6.0, Android 4.12.2.0, iOS 4.11.5.11, HarmonyOS 1.0.1.0, Linux 4.3.0.1 in five architectures, Apple TV 1.0.2.3.
Client 4.9.6.0 (2025-07-11) introduced dynamic delivery of API interface domains, which explains a rotating multi-host API list.
Client 4.9.0.5 (2023-11-21) added account#N login for per-device connection management and switched to the newer TAP virtual adapter driver.

The Windows installer payload ships TAP-Windows driver files (tap0901.sys, tap0901.cat, OemVista.inf, tapinstall.exe) for amd64/arm64/i386 in two variants (DriverVer 9.00.00.21 and 9.24.6.601), plus per-architecture sysproxy.exe.
Account concurrency is a purchased quantity from 1 to 2000 simultaneous devices, priced as plan price multiplied by concurrent-connection count.

The AJiaSu terms of service (version 2025-10-22) forbid sharing, providing or transferring network traffic or connection rights to others, and forbid reverse engineering, decompilation or disassembly.
Node identifiers have the form vvn-<number>-<number> and node listings expose an ok/other status column.
Connecting a node outside the account's entitlement returns `服务器不可用于用户组` (server not available for the user group) according to an observed client transcript.
The Android build is com.fvcorp.android.aijiasuclient by developer YOUDUN, 100K+ installs, updated 2026-09-03, and registration is restricted to mainland-China mobile numbers.
2718 distinct node IPv4 addresses covering 31 provinces were extracted from Android client 4.12.0.3 on 2026-07-26.

The vendored ajiasu-amd64-4.2.3.0.tar.gz in LoveToSpeedup unpacks to a binary whose sha256 (29e18740af8b69c6fa4f7b0ef269316b01e0400d7768583fc08044632be13b9f) equals the Linux client extracted in this project.
A Gitee API repository search for both `ajiasu` and `爱加速` returned zero results on 2026-10-23.
No 52pojie, linux.do, v2ex or Zhihu thread describing AJiaSu protocol reverse engineering was found; the only 52pojie hit is a membership request.
OpenAJS presents itself as Android client 4.11.10.0 with cv=20260525-1, i.e. it emulates a mobile profile while the current desktop build is 4.9.6.0; parameter sets therefore differ per platform.
Public code documents the AutoMatch endpoint (ClientApiVpnServer/AutoMatch with LocationLevel/LocationCode) but not the server-side node-selection semantics.
UDP mode, lwip mode and the TAP data path are not implemented in any public repository found; public work only drives the official client for those modes.
znicelya/ajiasu-proxy wraps the unmodified official CLI in per-connection containers and gates real-account use behind written compliance evidence.
PainterXIII/YouRan_Proxy commits a plaintext account/password pair in ajiasu/ajiasu.conf and a hard-coded password in ajiasu/install.sh; values are redacted here and must not be reused.
A typical third-party architecture is: official Linux client in proxy mode listening on 127.0.0.1:1080, with socat or a TCP forwarder republishing it on a public port.
The official site describes the service as mainland-China-only (31 provinces, 190+ cities, 2600-2700+ servers) and forbids use for accessing blocked overseas sites or cross-border networking.
